deep.reconstruction:
The page is one leaf of Gauss's table of decimal periods of 1/p for primes p (here p = 373, 367, 359, 353, 349, 347, 337, in descending order). The neighbouring pages continue the same table (397…379 before, 317…227 after), and a check-list of primes up to 997 has those already done struck out. This is the working manuscript behind the table of decimal expansions of fractions with prime denominators below 1000 that is printed in his collected Werke, vol. II. That table is tied to Disquisitiones Arithmeticae Arts. 312–318.

For each p Gauss writes 1/p = 0.00d1d2d3…, omitting the two leading zeros (1/p < 1/100 for p > 100). He groups the digits in tens and marks the groups I, II, III, … with Roman numerals. He stops once the beginning '…00' + first digits reappears; that is underlined (e.g. '…0563|002680', '…3297|002724', '…7|002881844', '…|0029'). The period length L = ord_p(10) is therefore (number of digits written before the repetition) + 2.

Period lengths read off the page:
- 373: 19 groups; repetition '002680' starts inside group XIX. L = 184 + 2 = 186 = 372/2.
- 367: 37 groups; '002724' recurs in group XXXVII. L = 366, so 10 is a primitive root mod 367.
- 359: 18 groups; the final '…1002' is the start of the repetition. L = 179 = 358/2.
- 353: L = 30 + 2 = 32 = 352/11.
- 349: 12 groups; '…7851|002865'. L = 116 = 348/3.
- 347: '…7|002881844'. L = 173 = 346/2.
- 337: 34 groups ending '…|0029'. L = 336, so 10 is a primitive root mod 337.

Implicit theory (my addition): L divides p−1. When 10 is a quadratic residue mod p, L divides (p−1)/2. By quadratic reciprocity (2/p)(5/p) = 1 for p = 373, 359 and 347; this is consistent with L = 186, 179 and 173.

When L is even, the second half of the period is the 9's complement of the first half, since 10^(L/2) ≡ −1 (mod p). The page bears this out (my verification):
- 373: group X/XI '6|9973190348|5254691689…' is the complement of '0026809651 4745308310'.
- 367: line 4 '2|997275204359 6730245…' complements '002724795640 3269754…' at position 184 = 183 + 1.
- 353: '8016|9971671388101983' complements '0028328611898016'.
- 349: '9971|3467048…' complements '0028653295 1…'.
- 337: the half-period falls in group XVII '884272|9970326409…', the complement of '00296735905044…'.
Gauss very likely used this to halve or check the labour; in Disquisitiones Art. 316ff he discusses exactly these shortcuts.

Independent check of the end of the 337 period (my computation): (10^336−1)/337 ≡ 89020771513353115727 (mod 10^22). So the period ends '…0089020 7715133531 15727', followed by the repetition '0029…'. This agrees with the page provided group XXXII is the corrected 9-digit '810089020' (Gauss struck out a leading digit; the bracket marks over XXXII/XXXIII look like correction marks) and the last group reads '15727|0029'.
errors: No arithmetical errors detected in the checked portions (half-period complements for 373, 367, 353, 349 and 337, and the period lengths for all seven primes).

Last line for 337: group XXXII shows a struck-out digit. Gauss corrected the group to the 9 digits '810089020', which is correct by computation. The transcribed last group '1572770029' would contain one 7 too many; the true continuation is '15727' followed by the repetition '0029'. This is either a transcription misreading or a small uncorrected slip in the manuscript.

results.what: Decimal periods of 1/p for p = 373, 367, 359, 353, 349, 347, 337, giving period lengths 186, 366, 179, 32, 116, 173, 336.
results.modern_name: Multiplicative order of 10 mod p / repetend of 1/p (full-reptend primes 367 and 337)
results.usually_credited_to: Tables by Gauss (Werke II), earlier J. H. Lambert, J. Bernoulli, Henry Goodwyn; later Burckhardt, Reuschle

results.what: Use or confirmation of the 9's-complement half-period property for even period length.
results.usually_credited_to: E. Midy (1836); stated earlier in substance by Gauss, Disq. Arith. Art. 316ff

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working sheet for Gauss's well-known, published table of decimal expansions of 1/p for primes below 1000 (Werke II; Disq. Arith. Arts. 312–318). It contains only routine computation; the only noteworthy feature is a visible self-correction in the 337 row.

checkable.asserts: first four groups of the 367 row
end of the 1/337 period is ...0089020 7715133531 15727 (supports correction of the last line)

transcription_corrections: 337, last line, group XXXII: the manuscript has a struck-out leading digit; the intended group is '810089020' (9 digits), not '8100890020'.
337, last group: the correct digits are '15727' + repetition '0029' (i.e. '157270029'); the transcribed '1572770029' has a spurious extra 7.
359 row: the final '…1002' is the beginning of the repetition (period 179); it is not underlined in the transcription but is evidently the recurrence marker.
